LXXII." with its title in two lines; then an italic summary paragraph with a decorated initial; then one paragraph of running text in one column with marginal notes at the left margin; no catchword or signature.

main_text.head: CAP. LXXII. Rhetoriani cur sic dicti. Error eorum quis fuerit.

p.i: Rhetorio' quodam exortam hæresin dicit nimium mirabilis vanitatis, qua omnes hæreticos rectè ambulare, & vera dicere affirmat, quod ità est absurdum, ut mihi incredibile videatur.

main_text.p: 1A Rhetorio.)Quis fuerit hic Rhetorius, nusquam alibi inuenio explicatum. Est tamen hæc hæresis Apellitarum furculus, ut ex Euseb. lib.5. cap.13. videtur colligi posse. Atque hi ipsi ab alijs, veluti à Damasceno, Lampetiani, à Lampetio quodam dicuntur, qui liberam cuique esse debere religionis, quam velit, & quam veram putat, professionem docent, quia nihil coactum aut inuitum Deo placet. Est quidem illud Epi-phanij in Apostolicis hæreticis dictum certissimum, ἐχ ἐπαναγκὲς ἢ διδαχῆς, ἀλλ' ἐκ προαιρέσεως ἡ δικαιοσύνη[?]. quod etiam Socrates libro 3. capite 25. probat, propterea tamen non debet quodlibet humani ingenij commentum admitti, &, ut Ἰουδαῖος[?] & probus numus recipi: sed ea tantum doctrina, quæ cælestis est, & verbo Dei consentiens, audienda. Immane verò est istud, quen-que hæreticum vera dicere in eo in quo censetur hæreticus, quæ dicendi ratio etiam in ipsis verbis contradictionem, ut aiunt, implicat, sic-que ipsa tollit & refutat. Cuius erroris nullum certè poteft esse fundamentum, nisi quis for-

page.notes: The chapter heading is set in the printed block above the summary; the headpiece is an ornament and is not transcribed. The mark after "Rhetorio'" in the summary is unclear and may be a printed reference sign. The margin note "A Rhetorio.)" begins with a large decorated A; it is read as a section letter. The Greek lines are read from a small, faded print and are uncertain letter by letter, so they are marked [?]; the first Greek word may be "οὐκ" rather than "ἐχ". The Greek word after "ut" is also uncertain. "Euseb." is read as Euseb. from the faint print. The last word on the page breaks at the printed hyphen "for-" and continues on the next page.
